questions.question: To add 3 998 + 2 500 mentally, Priya changes 3 998 into the friendly number 4 000 by adding 2. She then works out 4 000 + 2 500 = 6 500. What must she do next to get the correct sum?
options: Leave it as 6 500, because 2 is too small to matter
questions.explain: Priya added 2 that was never in the question, so she has to take that same 2 back off the answer: 6 500 − 2 = 6 498. The usual trap is adding the 2 back on instead of removing it.

questions.question: Liam adds 47 000 + 25 000 mentally by decomposing 25 000 into 20 000 + 5 000. He thinks: 47 000 + 20 000 = 67 000, and then adds the 5 000. What is the sum?
questions.explain: Decomposing means splitting one number into easy chunks and adding every chunk: 47 000 + 20 000 = 67 000, then 67 000 + 5 000 = 72 000. The common slip is stopping at 67 000 and forgetting the second chunk.

questions.question: Mia works out 8 000 − 2 996 mentally. She subtracts the friendly number 3 000 instead: 8 000 − 3 000 = 5 000. What is the difference for 8 000 − 2 996?
questions.explain: Mia took away 3 000, which is 4 more than 2 996, so she took away too much and must put 4 back: 5 000 + 4 = 5 004. The trap is subtracting the 4 again, which gives 4 996.

questions.question: Ravi wants to add 6 800 + 3 750 mentally. He decides to turn 6 800 into the friendly number 7 000 by adding 200 to it. To keep the sum exactly the same, what should he do before adding?
options: Add 200 to 3 750 as well, then add the two numbers
Subtract 2 000 from 3 750, then add the two numbers
Add 200 to the total at the very end
Subtract 200 from 3 750, then add the two numbers
questions.explain: When you build up one addend, you take the same amount off the other addend so the total does not change: 7 000 + 3 550 = 10 550, the same as 6 800 + 3 750. Adding 200 to both numbers makes the sum 400 too big.

questions.question: Find the sum 12 998 + 7 499 using friendly numbers and compensating.
questions.explain: Round up to 13 000 + 7 500 = 20 500, then take back the 2 and the 1 you added: 20 500 − 3 = 20 497. The common mistake is leaving the answer at 20 500 and never compensating.

questions.question: A Kelowna school raised $4 750 at its fall bottle drive and $2 990 at its winter bake sale. Using friendly numbers, how much did the school raise altogether?
questions.explain: Think $4 750 + $3 000 = $7 750, then subtract the extra $10 you added: $7 740. Adding the $10 back on instead of removing it gives the wrong total of $7 760.

questions.question: A BC Ferries vessel had travelled 306 000 km. Last year 149 000 of those kilometres were logged on a different route. Using friendly numbers, how many kilometres is 306 000 − 149 000?
questions.explain: Subtract the friendly 150 000: 306 000 − 150 000 = 156 000, then add back the 1 000 you over-subtracted, giving 157 000. Forgetting to add back leaves you at 156 000.

questions.question: Which mental method gives the correct value of 25 400 − 9 800?
options: Subtract 10 000 to get 15 400, then subtract 200 more, giving 15 200
Round both numbers down to 25 000 − 9 000, giving 16 000
Add 200 to 25 400 and subtract 200 from 9 800, giving 25 600 − 9 600 = 16 000
Subtract 10 000 to get 15 400, then add 200 back, giving 15 600
questions.explain: Subtracting 10 000 takes away 200 too much, so you add that 200 back: 15 400 + 200 = 15 600. Taking the 200 off a second time is the classic direction error in subtraction.

questions.question: Maya calculates 7 000 − 2 998 mentally. She thinks: 7 000 − 3 000 = 4 000, and 3 000 is 2 more than 2 998, so I subtract 2 more and get 3 998. What is wrong with her reasoning?
options: She already took away 2 too many, so she must add 2 back: the answer is 4 002
She should have rounded 2 998 down to 2 900, so 7 000 − 2 900 gives the answer 4 100
Nothing is wrong; 3 000 is 2 more than 2 998, so 2 more comes off and 3 998 is correct
She forgot to regroup the thousands, so 1 000 must go back on: the answer is 4 998
questions.explain: Taking away 3 000 removes 2 more than the question asks, so those 2 go back on: 4 000 + 2 = 4 002. Subtracting the extra amount a second time is the most common compensation error.

questions.question: A Surrey library had 128 000 books. Staff removed 39 000 worn-out books, then added 12 500 new ones. How many books does the library have now?
questions.explain: Subtract the friendly 40 000 to get 88 000, add back the 1 000 you over-subtracted to get 89 000, then add 12 500 for 101 500. Skipping that add-back step gives 100 500.

questions.question: A community centre in Nanaimo has a budget of $150 000. It spends $47 990 on a new playground and $22 010 on floor repairs. How much of the budget is left?
questions.explain: Notice that $47 990 and $22 010 pair up to a friendly $70 000, so $150 000 − $70 000 = $80 000. A common trap is subtracting only one of the two costs.

questions.question: Which expression has exactly the same value as 6 003 − 1 998?
questions.explain: In a subtraction you can shift both numbers by the same amount and the difference stays the same: adding 2 to each gives 6 005 − 2 000 = 4 005. Changing only 1 998 into 2 000 makes the difference 2 too small.
